data.summary: status/brief undercount the queue: items held back ONLY by schedule.max_parallel_tasks are counted as neither ready nor blocked, so tasks.total != done+running+ready+blocked. REPRO (home-simulator repo, 2026-10-01, schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4): before any claim, ddflow status -> tasks {total:45, done:0, running:0, ready:4, blocked:22} (19 dep-free items vanish: C6, 36.5a, 37.1a-e, 37.6a, 38.9, 38.10...). After claiming 4 items: ddflow --json status -> {total:45, done:0, running:4, ready:0, blocked:22} (sum 26), while ddflow --json next lists 41 blocked, those 19 with reason='state', detail='parallelism cap reached (schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4)'. So next and status disagree on the same snapshot. Effect: operator reading status/brief ('Ready now: 4') concludes only 4 items are startable and cannot see the other dep-free ones; brief prints 'These 4 are independent' implying the rest are not. EXPECTED: one classification shared by next/status/brief/board: report cap-held items explicitly (e.g. tasks.held_by_cap or ready_capped, or count them as ready with a 'cap reached' note), and keep the invariant total == sum of buckets (add a test asserting it). Secondary: human 'ddflow next' output lists dependency-blocked items first and buries the cap reason; when the cap is the only reason, say 'N more items are ready but held by max_parallel_tasks=K' in the summary line.
